newsitem.title: UK: PEARSON EYES BETTER FT MARGINS, S.AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: PEARSON EYES BETTER FT MARGINS, S.AFRICA.

text.p: Pearson, owner of the Financial Times, said on Monday that profit margins at the British newspaper were improving and getting better than those of its main rival, Dow Jones & Co's Wall Street Journal.

"Our trading margins are moving up nicely. By some measurements our margins have done better than at the Wall Street Journal, which is really the benchmark we've set," executive director David Bell told Reuters Financial TV.
"We are not happy with our (FT) margins, but they are improving," he added in an interview following Pearson's aquisition of a stake in South African business publications.

Bell said the purchase of the 50 percent stake in Business Day and Financial Mail for 11.5 million stg would be earnings enhancing. He would not elaborate. "We are not talking about the precise financial terms at this stage."
"We see great opportunities in South Africa...both in print and electronically as well," Bell said, adding that the two publications should benefit from Pearson's expertise.
"Our expertise, skill and some of our databases are relevant," he said, stressing the purchase would not bring about changes in the publications' style and coverage.
"We do not dictate -- and nor seek to dictate the political and the editorial view. That is entirely a matter of the editor," Bell said.
The acquisition fits Pearson's strategy of having a foothold in financial media in key markets, he added.

Business Day currently has daily sales of 40,200, while the weekly Financial Mail sells 31,000 per issue. Both publications will establish strong ties with the Britain's Financial Times whih will lend its international expertise, Perason said.
In view of the political changes in South Africa, Pearson opted for a joint venture with a local partner rather than taking full control over Business Day and Financial Mail.
"Because of the way the country is changing it would be wise to have a joint venture," Bell said.
He added that Pearson's continued to look at investments in the European business press such as in the Netherlands where it is in talks to buy privately-owned Financieele Dagblad.
"We are going to review the situation this week," Bell told Reuters after editorial staff at the Dutch newspaper voted on a potential acquistion by Pearson.
"We understand they were not enthusiastic about us or indeed anybody," Bell said.
Pearson also owns French business newspaper Les Echos, which itself is "doing very well" in terms of sales, but suffering from an overall sluggish French economy, Bell said.
"We are very pleased with the performance of Les Echos.. in what is a very difficult market," he said.
